original.guitar: John and Shane Fogerty (Legacy, 2025). John's CCR-era Rickenbacker is back in use; Les Paul style guitars on stage
original.amp: Not documented for Legacy. CCR-era sound: Kustom and modified Fender Vibrolux amps
original.notes: Re-recording on Legacy: The Creedence Clearwater Revival Years (August 2025), produced by John and Shane Fogerty. The studio gear is not published.

recipes.tips: Channel A is a Vibrolux-style blackface with a little edge, for the strummed rhythm. Channel B is a grittier tweed sound for the fuller parts. Let the open chords ring. For a fuller, rounder strum, switch to the middle position (both, humbucker).
recipes.why: Lodi is a mid-tempo country-rock song. The rhythm sits on a bright Fender-style amp just at the edge of breakup, with spring reverb and a very short slapback. The new version is fuller and more polished than the 1969 one, so the gain is a touch higher and the reverb a little bigger.

original.guitar: John and Shane Fogerty (Legacy, 2025). John's CCR-era Rickenbacker is back in use
original.amp: Not documented for Legacy. CCR-era sound: Kustom and modified Fender amps
original.effects: Treble-boosted edge, slapback, spring reverb (not documented)
original.notes: Re-recording on Legacy: The Creedence Clearwater Revival Years (August 2025), produced by John and Shane Fogerty. The studio gear is not published.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the intro lick and the fills, channel B for the solo. The treble boost gives that bright, snappy Rickenbacker-and-Kustom edge. Turn it off if it gets too sharp. Play the licks with a light, twangy touch near the bridge.
recipes.why: Fogerty's leads are bright and cutting rather than saturated: a Bassman-style tweed just breaking up, sharpened by a treble booster, with a slapback and spring reverb.
